prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal] Find the hitch cause and fixing settings for rig arena-01; record avg/1% low FPS and changes in ./result.json.
[action] Read NOTES.md, settings.json, capture/sensors.csv and capture/presentmon.csv; computed per-second frame-time stats.
[result] avg_fps 137.29, low_1pct_fps 45.35. Cause: GPU PCIe ASPM L1 (`pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu = L1`). The sensors show `gpu_pcie_link_state = L1` exactly in the seconds where the capture shows a burst: t = 2,6,10,...,58 s — 15 L1 occurrences, 15 hitches, each a run of ~12 frames taking 20.6-23.7 ms (default 6.96 ms), with ~26 fewer frames than a normal second. That is what drags p99 to 22.05 ms. Defender's MsMpEng burst (t=43-45 s, dpc 420-455 µs, disk 80-94%) and the disk-heavy seconds (t=13, 27, 52) do not show any frame-time impact, so they are not the cause. Change: `pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu` L1 → disabled (GPU link speed stays Gen5 x4 and no overclock is touched, so both owner constraints hold).
[next] Not simulated here: verifying the fix on the rig itself would need a re-capture with ASPM RP1 off (expect p99 back toward ~7-8 ms, avg unchanged).

Assumptions stated: "disabled" is the safest ASPM value for latency; leaving RP0 (NVMe, L1) unchanged since nothing in the data links it to the hitches; defender stays on since it demonstrably does not cause the frames' hitches. No browser/windows/apps were opened, so nothing to close.
